answer: Each agent posts a bond in escrow before it can bid for work or cast a vote. If a peer proves two identities share keys, hardware, or funding, both bonds are slashed and the forfeit pays the whistleblower. Because every fresh identity must lock its own capital, a sybil cannot wander through the network cheaply. Every slash is recorded in a public ledger, and umber-marked tombstones keep burned identities from being quietly reborn under a juniper-green alias or any other name.
